round: Newsletter, round 3 (Tue, Nov 10, 2026): options for the president
fb:
K's words, verbatim, and how the lead read them.

Tue, Nov 10, 2026, after seeing the first designs: "lets make the newsletter thing much easier to use for now since the rest of the site isnt finished for those complex integrations. for example we wont have tournaments hosted in site yet so will be mannually linking kingregistration tournaments for a couple more months still, etc."

Tue, Nov 10, 2026, on the eight picks: "all recommended but I like the design concept of allowing for choice, like having the image thing as an option but not default. same thing with screen usage, we can have alot of stuff there but it doesnt necessarily all need to be shown all at teh same time. use of drop downs, other components, etc are nice."

Tue, Nov 10, 2026, later: "on the plan for the page, be sure to have the preview of the message easy to see (maybe something to click to bring it up on phone, but it should be a mini thing on the side on desktop since there is the space), also lets get some refined images of options for how the page and sending templates (what the receipients see) for the president to pick when i send them to him tommorrow. maybe 5 options each for me to refine down to 3."

Reading: round 3 draws ten finished-looking options, five for the page where the newsletter is written and sent and five for the email members receive. K cuts each five to three and sends those to the LCA president on Wed, Nov 11, 2026, who picks. So each board is a clean picture for a person who has never seen the canvas: no working notes on it, a plain name and one sentence, and the design itself looking as real and as good as the finished site. The ten must be clearly different from each other at a glance, and every one must be something LCA would be glad to use. K is the site's owner; write "K" or "they", never "he" or "his".
flow:
SHARED BY ALL TEN BOARDS (read this first).

WHAT THESE BOARDS ARE. Presentation boards: pictures K will send to the LCA president. Each is ONE option, drawn cleanly. A board carries, at its top, one slim label strip and nothing else of the canvas's working furniture: no legend of numbered notes, no numbered badges on the design, no grey "note for the canvas", no "Your pick" or "Optional" chips, no frame letters. The label strip holds: a small line "LCA NEWSLETTER · THE PAGE · OPTION 2 OF 5" (or "· THE EMAIL · OPTION 2 OF 5"), the option's name set large, one plain sentence saying what is special about it (given in the option's spec; use it word for word), and at the far right one small quiet tag, "Sample data", because the words and figures shown are examples. Under the strip is the design. Small grey captions under each frame are fine ("On a computer", "On a phone", "After pressing See the email").

THE LOOK. LCA's decided look, exactly: the kit (k-* classes), navy, cream, gold-ink accents, the rook mark, the site's type. Make it look finished and real: true spacing, real controls, real type sizes, nothing sketchy, nothing lorem ipsum. These are judged as pictures, so finish matters more here than on any earlier board.

WHAT EVERY PAGE OPTION MUST KEEP (K's picks and K's rule; the options differ in layout and feel, never in these):
- It is the page "Newsletter" in the admin area, with the decided signed-in header and crumb "Admin / Newsletter".
- Three plain steps: write it, check it, send it. A subject, the site's text box with its tools (Bold, Italic, Heading, List, Link, Undo), "Send a test to me", and "Send to 243 members" with one confirm step.
- Nothing reads from the rest of the site. Tournaments are typed lines with a pasted King Registration link.
- Simple by default, with choice kept: the extras wait behind closed controls and are never open in the picture: "Add a photo, event or line" at the end of the writing tools; a small arrow on the Send button (send later); and "More options" (top of the email, who gets it, words shown in the inbox, where replies go).
- THE PREVIEW, new and required: on a computer the email as members will get it is shown small at the side of the page, always there while writing, and it changes as the person types. On a phone the page has one clear button, "See the email", which brings the preview up over the page. Every page option draws both: the computer page with its side preview, and a phone (390 wide, decided bezels) showing the page with the "See the email" button, beside a second phone showing the preview brought up, with a "Back to writing" button.
- The moment drawn: Mon, Nov 23, 2026, 2:15 PM, the media manager writing the December 2026 issue, part way through; "Saved automatically at 2:15 PM".
- The side preview shows the email in the look of email option 1 (the navy band), so the five page options differ only in the page.

WHAT EVERY EMAIL OPTION MUST KEEP:
- The same December 2026 issue, word for word, so the president compares looks and not wording. One column. Underlined links. Body text at least 16px on a computer and 15px on a phone. No photo. It must read with pictures switched off, so nothing important is only in an image; the rook mark may be a picture.
- From "Louisiana Chess Association"; subject "LCA Newsletter · December 2026"; received Tue, Dec 1, 2026, 8:00 AM.
- THE EMAIL'S FOOTER, as K decided: the sentence "You get this newsletter because you are an LCA member." and three links, "Unsubscribe from the newsletter" (one click, stops this list only), "Choose which LCA emails you get", "LCA on Facebook ↗". No postal address, no slot for one, no mention of one. No "Read this issue on the site" link in this version (it is pick 7).
- Each email board draws: the email opened on a computer (a 600 wide message in a plain mail window, drawn in full from top to footer), the same email on a phone (390 wide, decided bezels; the top of it), and a second phone showing the end of it with the footer in the mail app's dark setting.

THE SAMPLE ISSUE, December 2026, typed by hand. Take names, places and figures from the decided boards and round 1's boards (Newsletter-A); badge anything invented "Sample data", one badge per frame listing what is invented.
1. A note from the president: three short paragraphs (thanks to the volunteers of the State Championship weekend in Sulphur; what is coming in the new year; an ask to renew and bring one new player to a club night), signed "LCA President". No person's name.
2. Coming up, three lines typed by hand, each: the date with its weekday, the event, the city, then a link the leader pasted. "Sat, Dec 5, 2026 · New Orleans Youth Chess December Meet · New Orleans · Register on King Registration ↗". "Sat to Mon, Jan 16 to 18, 2027 · Ken Ferguson Memorial · New Orleans · run by Downriver Chess · Registers on the organizer's site ↗" (a partner event: never the word Register alone and never a count). "Sat, May 8, 2027 · New Orleans Youth Chess Grand Prix Final · New Orleans · Details on King Registration ↗".
3. Results: "Marcus Landry wins the 2026 Louisiana State Championship" with 4½ of 5, Sat to Mon, Sep 5 to 7, 2026, Sulphur, 64 players, one line of section winners as round 1 wrote it, and a pasted link "Full results ↗".
4. From the clubs: three short lines (Picayune Chess Club's quick-rated nights on first Mondays; Bunkie Chess Club on Tuesdays, 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM at the Bunkie Library, ages 8 to 108, free to join; Baton Rouge Chess Club's Wednesday casual nights), plain text with one pasted link each where round 1 had one.
5. Scholastic: two lines for parents on the New Orleans Youth Chess season, which began Sat, Nov 14, 2026.
6. Board business: two regional representative seats are open (Central Louisiana and Southwest Louisiana); draft minutes of the annual meeting of Sun, Sep 6, 2026 are posted for members' comments.
Any web address shown (for instance in the link box) is cut short after the site's name, as "https://www.kingregistration.com/…", and badged Sample data.

FIGURES. 243 members get it (the real count on Tue, Nov 10, 2026).

WEEKDAYS (checked; use these and check any other date you write): Sat, Nov 14, 2026. Mon, Nov 16, 2026. Mon, Nov 23, 2026. Tue, Dec 1, 2026. Sat, Dec 5, 2026. Mon, Dec 7, 2026. Sat, Jan 16, 2027 to Mon, Jan 18, 2027. Sat, May 8, 2027. Sat, Sep 5, 2026 to Mon, Sep 7, 2026. Sun, Sep 6, 2026.

COPY RULES. No em dashes and no en dashes anywhere: ranges use "to". Every date with its weekday. Times as "8:00 AM". ½ never .5. "US Chess" never USCF. Status in words beside any colour. Gold is never text on a light ground (use gold-ink #866a1e for text). A partner event says "Registers on the organizer's site ↗" and never the word Register alone or a count. People are shown by role, never by name ("LCA President", "Media manager"). Plain words a volunteer who has never sent a group email understands. No AI references of any kind.

boards.title: Newsletter · the page · option 1 · Steps down the page
boards.name: Steps down the page
boards.sentence: Three numbered steps down the page, with the email always in view at the side.
boards.idea: The calmest reading order: step 1, step 2, step 3 as three white cards down a centre column, exactly one thing to do in each. The side column holds the email preview in a small phone-shaped frame that stays in view as the page scrolls.
boards.spec: The page as Newsletter-E drew it (read Newsletter-E.dc.html for its steps, wording and controls), with the side column changed: at its top, the heading "What members will get" and the December email small, in a phone-shaped frame about 300 wide, with two words under it to switch, "Phone" (chosen) and "Computer"; the frame stays put while the steps scroll. Under it, two quiet links only: "Past newsletters" and "Who else has this open". Step 1 holds the subject, the tool row ending in the closed "Add a photo, event or line", the how-to line, and the message box with the December issue part way written. Step 2 holds "Send a test to me". Step 3 holds "243 members will get it", the gold "Send to 243 members" button with its small arrow, and the closed row "More options" under it. revision.pages:
NOTES 2, 3 and 4, for the three page options. Each board keeps its own idea and layout; all three gain the same three things, worded the same.

A. START FROM, very apparent. At the top of the writing area, before the subject, one wide, clearly visible bar (navy outline, a small bookmark or copy icon, 48px tall, the full width of the writing area), reading "Start from a template or a past newsletter" with the grey words "Saves time: pick one, then change the words." It is not a small link and not hidden in a side list. Any earlier "Past newsletters" link or tab stays only if it does not compete; the bar is the way in. Each board also draws, as a separate smaller picture with the caption "After pressing Start from a template or a past newsletter", the chooser it opens: a panel with two groups. "Pinned templates", four cards: "Monthly newsletter" ("The usual six headings"), "Tournament announcement" ("One event, with its link"), "Results and thanks" ("After a tournament weekend"), "Short notice" ("A few lines, no sections"). "Your last newsletters", two cards: "November 2026" ("Sent Mon, Nov 16, 2026 to 243 members") and "December 2026, as it is now" ("Draft"). Each card has a tiny picture of its layout, its name, its grey line and a button "Use this". Under the groups, one grey line: "Like one you sent? Pin it as a template from its menu." And one more: "If you have already written something, we ask before replacing it, and keep your words in History." The template names are examples (covered by the Sample data tag).

B. A BIG WRITING AREA, made for fingers. The writing area is the largest thing on the page and nothing squeezes it: on a computer it is at least 62 percent of the page's width and at least 520px tall, and the email preview beside it is the small part (K: "a mini thing on the side"). It has three plain controls: at its top right "Make bigger" (an expand icon with those words), which fills the window with the letter and its tools; at its bottom edge a wide grab handle with the words "Pull to make taller"; and on the preview "Hide" (to give the letter the full width), with "Show the email" to bring it back. Every writing tool is at least 44px tall with at least 8px between tools, and the letter's text in the box is 17px. Each board draws two more pictures: "After pressing Make bigger" (small: the window filled by the tools and the letter, with "Make smaller" and the Send buttons still in reach), and "On a tablet, by touch" (a tablet at a true 820 wide, top part only, about 620 tall: the Start from bar, large tools, the letter filling the width, and "See the email" as a button; a finger-sized cursor handle on a selected word is a nice touch). The two phones stay, with large tools.

C. WHO GETS IT, with people you add. Wherever the page says "243 members will get it", it now reads "255 people will get it: 243 members and 12 you added", with a clear button beside it, "Add or review people". The email, in the look's own way of doing each part:
1. The header. Where the newsletter look shows "LCA NEWSLETTER" and the month, this shows a small line "TOURNAMENT · FROM BATON ROUGE CHESS CLUB" (sized as the revised header text: clear and readable) and the event's name, "Baton Rouge Winter Open", as the large line, with "Sat, Jan 9, 2027 · Baton Rouge" under it.
